incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (Alberta), RSA 2000, c B-9, ss. 8(1), 10, 12, 24; prescribed Form 1 (Articles of Incorporation) under the Business Corporations Act Forms Regulation, Alta Reg 119/2000
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Corporate Registry, Service Alberta, Government of Alberta
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital under the Business Corporations Act (Alberta); a non-offering corporation may incorporate with nominal authorized capital. No escrow account or capital deposit rule applies; consideration for issued shares may be cash, property, or past services (s. 24 ABCA).

Anderson, President; Sarah L. Chen, Secretary; and David R. step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry (Service Alberta) via accredited NUANS search providers
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a NUANS name search request for the proposed corporate name and two alternate names. Verify trademark risks and Alberta corporate name availability. Obtain the official NUANS report within 90 days of the intended filing date and reserve the selected name, if desired, to secure exclusivity.
required_dossiers: Name reservation application (form if reservation is required)
Signed client authorization for name search
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused or conflicts with an earlier filing, re-file a fresh NUANS search on the next available alternate name and resubmit. A reconsideration letter may be submitted to Corporate Registry under s. 10(5) ABCA with supporting evidence of distinctiveness.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Execution of Articles of Incorporation (Form 1)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry / Accredited corporate registry agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft Form 1 stating the corporate name, registered office address in Alberta, full names and Alberta residential addresses of the first directors, share structure (e.g., an unlimited number of common shares without par value), restrictions on share transfer or business, and any additional provisions. Have the incorporator execute the articles, and obtain each director's signed consent to act.
required_dossiers: Directors' consents to act (each director signed)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If Corporate Registry issues a defect notice, cure the stated deficiency in the online filing and resubmit. For objections to name or provisions, amend Form 1 accordingly and refile; respond to any registry query within 30 days to preserve the filing date.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission, Fee Payment, and Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry online filing system (or authorized registry agent)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the completed Form 1 electronically and pay the prescribed incorporation fee. Upon approval, the registry issues a Certificate of Incorporation. Obtain the Alberta corporate access number and confirm the entity's legal name, jurisdiction, and effective date of creation.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried or rejected, correct identified deficiencies and resubmit. A partial fee refund may be available upon refusal, subject to Service Alberta's refund policy; escalate to the Registrar's office if processing exceeds the published SLA.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Establishment of the Registered Records Office Address
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Ensure the registered office and registered records office addresses are physically located in Alberta. If the records office address differs from or changes after the registered office stated in Articles, file the notice of registered office/registered records office with the registry and update the corporate minute book accordingly.
required_dossiers: Form 4 (Notice of Change of Registered Office / Registered Records Office Address) where applicable
Lease or occupancy documentation for the Alberta address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry rejects the address as non-physical or incomplete, provide a corrected civic address and municipal verification; refile within 15 days of the notice to avoid administrative cancellation or penalties.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Organizational Board Resolutions, By-law Adoption, and Share Issuance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporate Secretary and Board of Directors (internal corporate records)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting or obtain unanimous written consents to adopt By-law No. 1, approve the first board resolution (subscription, registered office, and officer appointments), issue the share certificate, approve officer banking authorizations, and create the corporate minute book with registers of directors, officers, and shareholders.
required_dossiers: Share certificate and share subscription records
Register of directors and Register of officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a director or officer does not sign the written resolution, re-circulate the consent or convene a duly noticed board meeting with a quorum; document any abstentions and record minutes to satisfy corporate law requirements.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration with the Canada Revenue Agency (CRA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency via Business Registration Online (BRO)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the corporation for a CRA Business Number (BN), corporate income tax account, GST/HST account (required once taxable supplies exceed CAD 30,000 per year; voluntary registration may be elected for input tax credits), and payroll account if employees will be hired. Provide the corporate legal name, registration date, and office address as per the Certificate of Incorporation.
required_dossiers: Registered office and records office address details
Corporate banking details (for refunds and direct deposit)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the CRA query or reject the account registration, review the BRO profile for name and address mismatches, correct the data, and resubmit. If the BN is delayed beyond five business days, contact CRA Business Enquiries with the corporation's access number.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Business Licence, WCB Registration, and Office Premises Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: City of Calgary / City of Edmonton Business Licensing; Workers' Compensation Board of Alberta (WCB)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for the municipal business licence covering the physical office premises in Alberta. If the corporation will employ individuals, register with the WCB and obtain clearance letters for workers' compensation coverage. Ensure the leased office complies with the Alberta Fire Code (fire extinguishers, alarms, and egress) and municipal occupancy requirements.
required_dossiers: Lease agreement or proof of lawful occupancy
Fire safety compliance inspection report (if required by municipality)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipality withholds the business licence due to zoning or fire-code deficiencies, obtain a development permit and complete the required fire safety upgrades, or relocate the office to a compliant premises and reapply. Appeals against licensing refusals must be filed within 14 days of the refusal notice.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable for ISIC 7020 (management consultancy and supply chain audit services); no Alberta industrial licensing board has jurisdiction. Office premises are governed by the local municipal business licensing authority in the municipality where the office is located.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable — non-industrial professional services; no Alberta manufacturing, industrial operations, or specialized operating permit is required for AEO certification and security auditing activities.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — administrative office activity is not listed as a mandatory or registrable activity under the Environmental Assessment (Mandatory and Exempt Activities) Regulation, Alta Reg 45/2017, or the Activities Designation Regulation; no EIA registration or approval is triggered.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable — the activity generates no industrial point-source wastewater discharge, no VOC emissions, and no hazardous waste streams. Office operations must comply with municipal sanitary sewer and solid waste by-laws; National Pollutant Release Inventory (NPRI) reporting thresholds are not triggered.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Alberta Fire Code compliance for office premises (fire extinguishers, alarm systems, and unobstructed egress); municipal building occupancy permit confirming structural load suitability for the office use; and Workers' Compensation Board of Alberta clearance letter (or exemption confirmation) where employees are engaged, together with an Occupational Health and Safety (OHS) workplace hazard assessment per the Alberta OHS Code.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada (ARC) — federal tax administration via Business Registration Online (BRO) and My Business Account (MyBA); Alberta Tax and Revenue Administration (TRA) — provincial corporate income tax administration (AT1 return); Alberta Corporate Registry — extra-provincial registration and Corporate Access Number (CAN); Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) — customs/export reporting (CARM portal) and AEO administration (PIP/CSA programs).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1 — Incorporate the business corporation under the Canada Business Corporations Act (federal) or the Alberta Business Corporations Act; if federally incorporated, register extra-provincially with the Alberta Corporate Registry to obtain the Corporate Access Number (CAN). Step 2 — Obtain the 9-digit Business Number (BN) from CRA via Business Registration Online (BRO) or Form RC1, selecting program accounts: RT (corporate income tax), RC (GST/HST), RP (payroll) and RZ (revenue). Step 3 — A foreign-owned corporation must designate a Canadian resident representative for service of notices, register for GST/HST where taxable supplies in Canada exceed the C$30,000 small-supplier threshold or are expected to, and file the T2 return within six months of its fiscal year-end. Step 4 — Register the same BN with Alberta TRA for provincial corporate income tax and file the AT1 return where a permanent establishment exists in Alberta.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation — the CA_CORP is a resident taxpayer subject to worldwide income taxation under Part I of the Income Tax Act and the Alberta Corporate Tax Act; no pass-through or disregarded-entity treatment is available for Canadian business corporations. Headline rates: federal general corporate rate 15%; Alberta general corporate rate 8%; combined general rate 23%. The federal small business deduction (9% federal / 2% Alberta) is denied because a foreign-owned corporation is not a Canadian-controlled private corporation (CCPC).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada has no check-the-box regulation; corporations are per se entity-level taxpayers. Relevant elections: (i) ETA s.156 — election by closely related registrant corporations to treat taxable intercompany supplies as made for nil consideration, reducing GST/HST cash-flow frictions; (ii) ETA s.240(1) — voluntary GST/HST registration by a small supplier to claim input tax credits; (iii) GST/HST filing-period election (annual versus quarterly or monthly); (iv) hybrid-mismatch exposure is constrained by ITA ss.18.2–18.4 and the Canada-US Treaty Art. IV(7) fiscally transparent entity ordering rule where interposed flow-through vehicles are used.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST (Goods and Services Tax) — federal value-added tax under Part IX of the Excise Tax Act; Alberta is a non-participating province with no provincial sales tax (PST), so no HST applies; the effective indirect tax on taxable supplies made in Alberta is 5% GST.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: C$30,000 — GST/HST small-supplier threshold (ETA s.240); registration is mandatory where taxable supplies made in Canada exceed C$30,000 in any single calendar quarter or the aggregate of four consecutive calendar quarters; zero-rated exports count as taxable supplies for threshold purposes but attract no actual tax; non-resident B2B audit service providers must register once this threshold is exceeded.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping or mandatory e-invoicing regime exists at the federal or Alberta level. Canada is implementing an optional pan-Canadian e-invoicing framework (Peppol PINT standard, announced in Budget 2023; voluntary participation as of 2025). Mandatory electronic filing: GST/HST registrants with annual gross revenue above C$1 million must file and remit electronically (GST/HST NETFILE plus electronic payment). For customs trade flows, the CBSA Assessment and Revenue Management (CARM) portal is now the mandatory digital channel for import/export accounting and duty/GST collection; AEO (PIP/CSA) participants must maintain EDI/API connectivity with CBSA.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods: zero-rated under Schedule VI, Part V (ETA ss.20–22) where the supplier ships or delivers the goods to a non-resident recipient and the goods are exported as soon as reasonably possible, evidenced by transport documents and export declarations. Services: an AEO supply-chain audit, consulting or professional service supplied to a non-resident who is not registered for GST/HST is zero-rated under Schedule VI, Part V, para 23(b), provided the service does not relate to (i) real property situated in Canada, (ii) tangible personal property situated in Canada at the time the service is performed, or (iii) an individual present in Canada; that portion of the service physically performed against Canadian-sited inventory or premises does not qualify.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration — CBSA export reporting (CARM/CAED electronic filing) for physical goods
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill issued by the carrier evidencing exit of goods from Canada
Inward Remittance Certificate / bank SWIFT credit advice evidencing FX repatriation of export proceeds
Commercial invoice and executed service contract (zero-rated AEO audit services)
Foreign recipient's non-resident status evidence (foreign business registry extract or foreign VAT/GST number)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA and CBSA may conduct joint verification of exported quantities, valuations and service-recipient status. A zero-rating claim must be substantiated within the 6-year records retention period (ETA s.286). Denial or overstatement triggers clawback of unremitted GST at 5% plus prescribed daily interest (ETA s.280) and civil penalties: ETA s.285 false-statement penalty — the greater of C$100 and 25% of the net tax misstatement; ITA s.163(2) gross-negligence penalty — 50% of additional tax payable for wilful blindness or negligence; criminal exposure under ETA s.327 and Criminal Code s.380(1) where intent is established. The CRA reassessment window is four years, unlimited where a return contains misrepresentation attributable to neglect, carelessness or wilful default (ETA s.298(2)). CBSA may also levy administrative monetary penalties (AMPS) of up to C$25,000 per export-reporting contravention and suspend or revoke AEO (PIP/CSA) certification for systemic non-compliance.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) / Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) — OSFI supervises banks but has no foreign-exchange-control mandate; Canada does not operate a central exchange-control approval agency.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains full current-account and capital-account convertibility under IMF Article VIII. No central-bank permit or exchange-control approval is required for equity injections, loan repatriation, dividend remittance, or trade settlements. Profit remittance is unrestricted in law, but Canadian withholding tax under Part XIII of the Income Tax Act (statutory 25%, treaty-reduced) applies to dividends, interest, and royalties paid to non-residents, and FATCA/CRS reporting and a valid CRA non-resident tax number may be required for streamlined remittance. CAD/USD and other major-currency conversions are freely transacted by the banking system at commercial rates.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Not applicable. Canada imposes no statutory export-proceeds surrender obligation, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no repatriation time limit. Exporters may lawfully retain foreign currency in Canadian or offshore foreign-currency accounts. Cross-border currency or monetary instrument movements in excess of CAD 10,000 are reportable to FINTRAC, but that reporting is not a conversion or surrender requirement.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium as a global payment pipeline extension, Low as a primary transactional banking solution. Canada does not recognise the European EMI/e-money passport. A non-resident EMI can only take Canadian-dollar deposits or issue e-money to the corporate client if it obtains a Canadian bank licence under the Bank Act or an order of the Minister of Finance; in ordinary practice, foreign EMIs such as Wise operate as FINTRAC-registered money services businesses (MSBs) and use a Canadian Schedule I bank for actual CAD clearing, custodial balances, and settlement. Using an unlicensed offshore EMI for primary corporate deposits is legally unavailable, exposes the operating entity to uninsured-funding risk, and may trigger enhanced scrutiny from OSFI and FINTRAC.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: There is no federal or Alberta statutory requirement for directors to appear physically at a bank branch for every corporate account. Canadian banks apply risk-based KYC: live video verification with government-issued photo identity is accepted for standard operating accounts, but high-value, multi-jurisdiction, or supply-chain-audit accounts with non-resident directors and complex ownership often require either a physical interview at the bank or a notarised identity attestation verified through a Canadian consulate or an acceptable international apostille process. The Alberta Business Corporations Act requires a registered office and an Alberta-registered agent, but that does not waive the bank's KYB/UBO, source-of-funds, and signing-authority verification procedures.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Complex or opaque ownership with non-resident holding companies or discretionary trusts
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Legal-certified organisation chart; register of directors; UBO registry extract; trust deed or trust attestation; source-of-funds statement from the ultimate beneficial owner; audited financial statements of intermediate holding vehicles.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch between declared AEO/customs-security-audit service scope and inbound wire payment narratives
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed client service agreement; detailed invoice ledger; Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) Partners in Protection (PIP) certificate; AEO-like security audit report; customs broker engagement letter; and a list of completed audit projects with reference numbers.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payments to or from high-risk or sanctioned jurisdictions within the supply-chain client base
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Denied-party/sanction screening logs for all counterparties; bills of lading and Customs Entry documents; Incoterms and contractual chain; independent international trade compliance opinion; and enhanced due-diligence file demonstrating no sanctioned country predicate.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Rapid ‘pass-through’ or split inbound/outbound transaction profile characteristic of trade-based money laundering
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: 13-month projected cash-flow model; customer and supplier list linked to MT103 confirmations; contract and invoice chain; internal supply-chain-security policy; annual independent audit of the AEO security program; and a written explanation of payment timing cycles.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Politically Exposed Person (PEP) or prominent public function holder in shareholder structure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: PEP-specific risk assessment; source-of-wealth declaration in prescribed form; independent legal counsel opinion; senior-management approval memorandum; and ongoing monitoring protocol identifying transactions with the PEP-related account.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unexpected high-value equity injection without corporate documentary support
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Directors' resolution authorising share issuance; Canada Revenue Agency corporate filings; shareholders' register update; share certificate specimens; and bank reference letter confirming the remitter's source of funds.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity or shareholder-loan capital is routed by international wire transfer using the SWIFT MT103 (or Fedwire/CHIPS for USD funding) to the corporate CAD or USD account at a Canadian Schedule I bank. The payment narrative should state the purpose as ‘share capital contribution’, ‘equity contribution’, or ‘shareholder loan advance’ and include the corporate legal name, jurisdiction of incorporation, and Canadian bank account instructions (institution number, transit number, and SWIFT BIC). Canada does not operate a fixed purpose-code taxonomy; the bank records the narrative and may assign an internal transaction code for FINTRAC reporting. For CAD clearing, the settlement leg uses Payments Canada Rails, including Lynx for high-value real-time gross settlement and ACSS for batch automated clearing. The bank must verify the share register, directors' resolution, and source of funds before releasing the full balance for operational disbursement; no Bank of Canada approval or exchange-control permit is required.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade payments for supply-chain audit services, customs compliance work, and operational consulting are cleared through (i) SWIFT MT103 for standard single customer credit transfers, (ii) SWIFT MT700/MT701 for documentary Commercial Letters of Credit issued or confirmed by the Canadian bank, and (iii) SWIFT MT202 for bank-to-bank cover when a separate cover payment is required. Domestic disbursements in Canadian dollars use Payments Canada Rails: Lynx for urgent high-value payments, Real-Time Rail for immediate retail/API payments, and ACSS for batch electronic funds transfer. Trade settlements require supporting invoice packs, service certificates, CBSA or customs documentation, and, where applicable, a letter of credit or documentary collection instruction. Payment clearing is unrestricted; no Bank of Canada permission is required. For USD-denominated disbursements, the bank may use correspondent banking via Fedwire/CHIPS with the bank's SWIFT BIC.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright CAD/USD forward contracts with tenors aligned to export/import settlement dates
FX cross-currency swaps (CAD/USD and major-currency pairs) for long-horizon balance-sheet hedging
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for minor or emerging-market currencies involved in non-Canadian supply-chain counterparties
Vanilla FX options and collar/range-forward structures for purchased exposure protection
Cross-currency interest-rate swaps where trade receivables are denominated in a different major currency

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days following each anniversary of incorporation or amalgamation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing may trigger a CAD 100 penalty and, on continued default, administrative strike-off by the Registrar under the Business Corporations Act.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before the last day of the sixth month after the corporation's taxation year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of unpaid tax, plus 1% per month up to 12 months; can adversely affect AEO/Customs compliance status.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A distributing corporation under the Alberta Business Corporations Act must appoint an auditor; a non-distributing corporation is exempt only if all shareholders waive the audit in writing. No revenue or asset threshold applies.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS for publicly accountable/distributing enterprises; Canadian Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE) for private companies under CPA Canada Handbook.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Alberta Business Corporations Act does not require a separate annual UBO confirmation filing; share transfers must be recorded in the register as they occur. Federal CBCA individuals with significant control rules apply only to federally incorporated entities.
